ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
S-Corporation designs its logo by linking together $4$ semicircles along the diameter of a unit circle. Find the perimeter of the shaded portion of the logo.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a circular logo, whose entire outer boundary is a circle; inside the circle there is a white S-shaped dividing line, separating the gray shaded region from the white region. According to the problem statement and the figure, this S-shaped internal dividing line is composed of 4 semicircular arcs connected along the diameter of the unit circle. Reasoning: The radius of the unit circle is 1, so the circumference of the outer circle is 2π. The internal dividing line is composed of 4 semicircles; the diameter of each semicircle is equal to half the diameter of the large circle, so the radius of each small semicircle is 1/2. The arc length of one small semicircle is π·(1/2)=π/2, and 4 together total 4·π/2=2π. The boundary of the shaded part includes the outer circumference and the internal S-shaped boundary, so the total perimeter is 2π+2π=4π.

raw_record.question_text: S-Corporation designs its logo by linking together 4 semicircles along the diameter of a unit circle. Find the perimeter of the shaded portion of the logo.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a unit circle whose shaded region has two kinds of boundary: the entire outer circumference of the unit circle, and the S-shaped interior boundary made from 4 linked semicircles. From the text, the circle is unit radius, so the outer circle contributes 2π. From the image/text, each of the 4 interior semicircles has diameter equal to half the big diameter, so radius 1/2; each contributes arc length π(1/2)=π/2. The interior boundary contributes 4·π/2=2π. Add outer and interior boundary lengths: 2π+2π=4π.

method.method_draft: Use the 180-degree symmetry visible in the diagram. The shaded part can be viewed as two congruent shaded lobes. Compute the perimeter of one lobe: its outer boundary is one semicircle of the unit circle, length π, and its inner S-boundary consists of two of the smaller semicircles, each of radius 1/2, contributing 2·(π/2)=π. Thus one lobe has perimeter π+π=2π. Since there are two congruent shaded lobes, the total shaded perimeter is 2·2π=4π.
